frase_gancho.texto: Villages beside the lakes, women made of clay, and a volcano that buried everything.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: Here begins village life in central Mexico. The first communities settled beside the lakes of the Basin, planted corn, beans, and squash, and shaped pottery. At Tlatilco appear the figurines of wide-hipped women, the acrobats, and the masks with two faces. They speak of fertility and duality. Later comes Cuicuilco, with its circular base and one of the oldest images of the Old God of Fire. Its story ends when the Xitle volcano covers it in lava, and the population moves toward Teotihuacán.
